narrative:
Based on the analysis of your academic profile, the system has estimated a 38% chance that you will fail your final year. Since this exceeds the 10% threshold used to identify students who may need additional support, you are required to enroll in remedial courses. This decision is not a punishment — it is designed to help you succeed.

Three factors most strongly shaped this prediction. The most influential was your number of past failures, which actually worked in your favor: having no prior failed classes is a positive signal that pushed the prediction toward passing. This is encouraging and suggests you have the foundational ability to succeed.

However, the second most important factor — your weekly study time — raised concern. You currently study less than two hours per week, whereas students who are not required to take remedial courses typically study between two and ten hours weekly. This gap is significant and directly increases your predicted risk of failing.

The third factor is your aspiration to pursue higher education, which also worked in your favor. Wanting to continue your studies beyond high school is a motivating force that the model recognizes as a protective factor.

Ultimately, the low study time is the clearest area where change can make a real difference. Despite your clean academic record and your ambitions for the future, not dedicating enough time to your studies is putting those goals at risk.

You should use the remedial courses as an opportunity to build stronger study habits. Increasing your weekly study time, even modestly, could significantly improve your chances of finishing the year successfully.

prompt:

The dataset contains information on students from two Portuguese high schools.

The target variable is whether the student will fail their final year.

Protected attributes sex, age and health were not used to make the machine prediction.

2. TECHNICAL EXPLANATION: SHAP VALUES
A SHAP value tells you how much a feature influenced the prediction (larger absolute value means a stronger influence) and its direction: positive pushes toward failing the final year, negative toward passing the final year. Below are the top 3 features by absolute SHAP value.

3. STUDENT PROFILE

5. YOUR NARRATIVE TASK
Write a detailed narrative explanation tailored to this non-technical reader that MUST explain:
1) The model's predicted probability of failing the final year and what this means for the student.
2) Why the student is obliged to take remedial courses: which features were most important in driving this prediction and why (focus on the ranking of most important features).

CONSTRAINTS:
